reviewer: Codex implementation self-review; advisory only, product-owner acceptance required
rationale: The slice preserves the intended authority boundary: Go remains the only native Target and outbox writer, PostgreSQL remains authoritative for business and delivery facts, and Temporal stores only bounded orchestration history. The dispatcher claims without spanning a Temporal RPC, fences every acknowledgement, preserves per-aggregate order, retries availability failures, recovers expired leases, and quarantines unsupported or exhausted events. The Workflow uses stable versioned contracts, deduplicates at-least-once delivery, rejects cross-aggregate signals, exposes an operational query, and continues as new with carried bounded state. A real Target commit survived a live Temporal outage and delivered after recovery; duplicate delivery, captured-history replay, container recreation, real PostgreSQL fencing, race tests, vet, typecheck, and build all passed. Review remediation also made API-key authentication TLS-only and bound the local Temporal ports to loopback. Independent review, production operations, failed-event repair, the inherited 24-test baseline, Graph/Run work, and every ship action remain explicit gates.
conditions: Treat this as advisory acceptance for product-owner review, not permission to commit, merge, deploy, release, or announce.
Keep PostgreSQL and the Go Domain API authoritative; do not let Workflow query state become product truth.
Add an audited failed-event inspection and repair path before production operations rely on this dispatcher.
Define production Temporal topology, worker packaging, readiness, metrics, backup, and recovery before enabling the worker outside controlled environments.
Resolve or formally baseline the inherited repository-wide runtime failures before claiming a release candidate.
Start Graph activation and Run execution only through a separately contracted vertical slice.
